articles.title: Leaf-derived Coatings Help Hydrochar Resist Oxidation, Pointing Toward More Durable Soil Carbon Storage
articles.description: A research team has found that a naturally formed, water-repellent coating helps hydrochar resist chemical oxidation, revealing how plant leaf chemistry could influence the durability of carbon-rich materials intended for soil applications. The coating contains alkyl carbon derived from leaf waxes and cutin, with its composition varying among plant species. Removing it increased carbon loss during laboratory oxidation tests for hydrochar made from lotus leaves, palm leaves, and pine needles, while leaving thermal stability largely unchanged. These findings could guide biomass selection and processing strategies that preserve protective surface chemistry, potentially improving hydrochar's usefulness for soil carbon storage.
